subject: Communication
title: Data Privacy: Your Digital Footprint
description: One-minute skill: Data Privacy: Your Digital Footprint.

hook.text: Every click, search, and like creates a data trail. Companies know your habits better than your closest friends.

buildup.text: Data brokers collect and sell personal profiles. Your digital footprint is bought and sold thousands of times yearly.

discovery.text: Cambridge Analytica used Facebook data from 87 million users to target political ads. Data became a weapon.

twist.text: GDPR gave Europeans data rights. But most people still click 'accept all cookies' without reading a single word.

climax.text: Media literacy now includes data literacy: understanding what you share, who collects it, and how it's used.

punchline.text: If the service is free, you're the product being sold.

details.summary: Every online action creates data that is collected, analyzed, and monetized. Your digital footprint reveals your location, relationships, interests, health, finances, and political views.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding your digital footprint empowers you to make informed choices about what data you share and with whom.
takeaways: Every online action generates collectible personal data
Your digital footprint reveals far more than you realize
This data enables targeting, pricing manipulation, and surveillance

faq.question: What data do companies actually collect about you?
faq.answer: Location data from your phone, browsing history, purchase records, social connections, search queries, app usage patterns, email content in some cases, voice recordings from smart devices, and biometric data.

faq.question: What practical steps protect your digital privacy?
faq.answer: Use privacy-focused browsers and search engines. Review app permissions regularly. Use a VPN for sensitive browsing. Read privacy policies before accepting. Minimize data sharing on social platforms. Use different passwords with a password manager.
